title: Being agile and doing agile
blurb: Explain the difference between being agile and doing agile, and spot which one a situation describes.
question: A team runs every agile event and uses all the agile terms, but cannot change a single priority without a manager's sign-off. Is it being agile, doing agile, or both?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile separates two ideas. Doing agile is the practical side: applying agile frameworks, following agile processes, using agile techniques and adopting agile terminology. Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that mindset to your work, within appropriate levels of self-management. In plain English: doing agile is what you can see a team do; being agile is how the team thinks and how much freedom it has to act on that thinking.

The book makes a sharp point: if agile thinking is not instilled and people are not given suitable freedom, calling processes, frameworks or techniques 'agile' is meaningless, because the organization still cannot be agile. That gap between the label and the reality is what 'being versus doing agile' describes. Note the word 'allowed' in the definition of being agile: the mindset needs permission from the organization, not just good intentions from the team.

teach.h: The two contrasts the book draws
head: Contrast
Being agile
Doing agile alone

teach.body: Being agile lets teams adapt to change and think critically about their work. Doing agile on its own can trap a team in routine: it follows the framework's steps rigidly without understanding why those steps exist. When the situation changes, a routine-bound team keeps running the ceremony; an adaptable team asks whether the ceremony still serves its purpose.

teach.h: Contrast 2: long-term impact versus short-term mechanics
teach.body: Being agile leads to a cultural shift and long-term organizational resilience. Doing agile alone focuses on the mechanics of agile practices: it may bring short-term efficiency gains, but they lack sustainable impact. So when an exam option talks about lasting cultural change, it describes being agile; when it talks about quick efficiency from new mechanics, it describes doing agile alone.

root.label: The team uses agile events and terms

teach.body: Brackenford Council's revenues team adopted Scrum a year ago. It holds every event and talks in story points, yet any change to the backlog order still needs the head of service's signature, so resident feedback waits weeks. Project manager Aisha Bello agrees decision boundaries with the board, recorded in a delegation matrix. Within them, the product owner reorders the backlog and the team adapts each iteration. The mechanics stayed the same; what changed was the team's freedom to be agile.

teach.text: Being agile is not 'following the agile framework carefully'. Rigid framework use without the 'why' is the routine side of doing agile alone. Being agile means thinking in an agile way AND being allowed to act on it within appropriate self-management.

items: Doing agile: applying frameworks, following processes, using techniques, adopting terminology.
Being agile: thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply it within appropriate self-management.
Adaptability vs routine: being agile adapts and asks why; doing agile alone may follow steps rigidly.
Long-term vs short-term: being agile brings cultural shift and resilience; doing agile alone gives short-term gains.
Agile labels mean little if people are not free to be agile.

summary: You can now define doing agile (frameworks, processes, techniques, terminology) and being agile (agile thinking plus the freedom to apply it within appropriate self-management). You can also use the two contrasts, adaptability versus routine and long-term impact versus short-term mechanics, to classify a situation.

A.q: Which describes 'doing agile' in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Thinking in an agile way with freedom to act on it
Applying agile frameworks, processes and techniques
Building a culture of long-term resilience
Adapting work after thinking critically about it
A.why: Doing agile is the practical application of agile frameworks, processes and techniques, plus adopting agile terminology (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply it is the definition of being agile.
whyNot.2: Long-term resilience is what being agile leads to, in the long-term versus short-term contrast.
whyNot.3: Adapting and thinking critically is the being-agile side of adaptability versus routine.

A.q: Which describes 'being agile' in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Adopting agile terminology across all teams
Holding every event the chosen framework defines
Thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply it
Following one agile framework closely and consistently
A.why: Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that mindset within appropriate levels of self-management (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Adopting agile terminology is part of doing agile.
whyNot.1: Running a framework's events is the practical, doing side of agile.
whyNot.3: Close adherence to a framework is doing agile; on its own it risks rigid routine.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being [?] to apply this mindset to your work within appropriate levels of self-management.
A.why: The definition stresses being allowed: the organization must give people the freedom to apply the mindset (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Training helps adoption, but the definition is about permission to act, not training.
whyNot.1: Being instructed is the opposite of the self-management the definition describes.
whyNot.2: Certification is not part of the definition of being agile.

B.q: A team follows its framework's steps exactly, but cannot explain why the steps exist and does not change them when circumstances change. Which contrast in PRINCE2 Agile does this illustrate?
B.why: Doing agile alone may limit teams to following frameworks rigidly without understanding the 'why'; being agile lets them adapt and think critically (2.3.1).

whyNot.1: This contrast is about lasting cultural impact versus short-term efficiency, not rigid steps.
whyNot.2: Values and principles are layers of the Agile Onion, not a being-versus-doing contrast.
whyNot.3: Projects versus BAU is about where agile is used, not about mindset.

B.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, what does being agile lead to that doing agile alone does not?
options: A cultural shift and lasting resilience
Guaranteed faster delivery from the framework
B.why: Being agile leads to a cultural shift and long-term organizational resilience; doing agile alone may give short-term gains without sustainable impact (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Short-term efficiency gains are what doing agile alone may provide.
whyNot.2: Adopting terminology is part of doing agile.
whyNot.3: The book warns that adopting a framework does not by itself guarantee faster delivery (2.3).

B.q: An organization renames its teams 'squads', buys a Kanban tool and holds daily stand-ups, but managers still decide every change. How would PRINCE2 Agile describe this?
B.why: The tools, events and labels are doing agile; without freedom to apply agile thinking, the organization is not being agile (2.3, 2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Being agile needs freedom to act within self-management, which is missing here.
whyNot.1: Being agile is absent because people are not allowed to make decisions.
whyNot.3: Scaling is about many teams and products; nothing here describes multi-team alignment.

C.q:
Which two statements about being and doing agile are correct?
1. Doing agile includes adopting agile terminology.
2. Being agile means following a framework as closely as possible.
3. Doing agile alone may give short-term efficiency gains without sustainable impact.
4. Being agile is mainly about choosing the right techniques.
C.why: Terminology is part of doing agile (1), and doing agile alone may give short-term gains that lack sustainable impact (3) (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: close framework adherence is doing agile and risks rigid routine.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: being agile is about mindset and freedom, not framework adherence or technique choice.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: choosing techniques is part of doing agile.

C.q: Which pairing correctly matches the 'long-term impact versus short-term mechanics' contrast?
options: Being agile: framework mechanics; doing agile: resilience
Being agile: cultural shift; doing agile alone: short-term gains
Being agile: short-term gains; doing agile: cultural shift
Being agile: new terminology; doing agile alone: lasting change
C.why: Being agile leads to cultural shift and long-term resilience; doing agile alone focuses on mechanics that may give short-term gains (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: This reverses the contrast: mechanics belong to doing agile, resilience to being agile.
whyNot.2: This swaps the two sides of the contrast.
whyNot.3: Terminology belongs to doing agile, and doing agile alone lacks lasting impact.

C.q: At Lindell Pharmacy Group, the board wants change that lasts after the consultants leave. The team already runs all the Scrum events but needs approval for every priority change. What should change, and why?
options: Add more events, because routine builds resilience
Change framework, because Scrum lacks lasting impact
Write a fuller plan, because control makes change last
Grant agreed decision freedom, because being agile lasts
C.why: The team is doing agile but not being agile. Giving it freedom within agreed self-management enables being agile, which leads to cultural shift and long-term resilience (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: More events add mechanics; doing agile alone lacks sustainable impact.
whyNot.1: Swapping frameworks is still doing agile; the missing piece is freedom to apply the mindset.
whyNot.2: More up-front control reduces the self-management that being agile needs.

reteach.title: Learning the steps versus dancing
reteach.question: Why can a team that does everything agile still not be agile?

blocks.body: Learning dance steps is doing: you can see them, copy them and count them. Dancing is being: hearing the music and adjusting as it changes. A team that knows every agile step but is not allowed to adjust to the music is doing agile without being agile. PRINCE2 Agile wants both: the structure of the steps and the freedom to respond.

blocks.text: An option that defines being agile as following a framework closely is wrong. That is doing agile, and on its own it risks rigid routine.

explain.body: Doing agile is the practical application of agile: frameworks, processes, techniques and terminology (2.3.1).

test.why: Adopting agile terminology is one of the four elements of doing agile (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Freedom to apply agile thinking is part of being agile.
whyNot.2: Cultural shift is what being agile leads to.
whyNot.3: Critical thinking and adaptation describe being agile.

explain.body: Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that thinking within appropriate levels of self-management (2.3.1).

test.q: Which phrase is part of the PRINCE2 Agile definition of being agile?
options: Using the techniques of one framework
Within the steps that the chosen framework sets out
test.why: Being agile is applying the agile mindset within appropriate levels of self-management (2.3.1).

whyNot.1: Following agile processes is doing agile.
whyNot.3: Working inside a framework's steps describes doing agile.

explain.body: Being agile lets teams adapt and think critically. Doing agile alone may leave them following the framework rigidly without knowing why (2.3.1).

test.q: A team keeps its usual retrospective format even though it no longer surfaces any improvements. Which side of 'adaptability versus routine' does this show?
options: Being agile, because the team works consistently each time
Doing agile, because steps continue without the why
Being agile, because retrospectives are held
Doing agile, because the team has adapted
test.why: Running a step that no longer serves its purpose is routine without the 'why', the doing-agile side (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Consistency without purpose is routine, not adaptability.
whyNot.2: Holding an event is doing agile; it does not show the mindset.
whyNot.3: The team has not adapted; it kept the old format.

explain.body: Being agile leads to cultural shift and long-term resilience. Doing agile alone may give short-term efficiency gains that lack sustainable impact (2.3.1).

test.q: Which outcome does PRINCE2 Agile link to doing agile alone?
test.why: Doing agile alone focuses on mechanics that may provide short-term efficiency gains but lack sustainable impact (2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Long-term resilience comes from being agile.
whyNot.1: Cultural shift is linked to being agile.
whyNot.3: Freedom to decide is part of being agile.
